newsitem.title: MEXICO: Strong demand for TMM's $200 mln note.
newsitem.headline: Strong demand for TMM's $200 mln note.

text.p: Demand was strong for Mexican shipping and transportation company, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana SA's recently placed $200 million senior note, assistant Finance Director Armando Torres said on Monday.
Demand for the note, placed in the Yankee market, reached about $350 million, Torres said.
Most of TMM's debt is denominated in U.S. dollars, but about 95 percent of the company's total revenues are in dollars, giving the company a natural hedge, Standard & Poor's said.
"We placed the $200 million in its entirety and we had orders for about $350 million," he said. "The market was anxious for the issue."
The note, due November 15, 2006, had a nominal yield of 10 percent, and a yield to maturity of about 10.06 percent, Torres said. It was placed last week.
The senior note is to be used for general corporate purposes and to pay down an outstanding medium-term note, worth $75 million, that comes due in October 1997, the company said.
Standard & Poor's had assigned a rating of BB to the note.
-- Robert Kozak, Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
